comparison: Perfect claim overlap (C86-C96) on structural database searches for β-layers. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on systematic search criteria and identification in existing structures. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting expansion of the analysis and assessment of previously unnoticed β-layers in PDB, indicating the presented analysis is incomplete.

Perfect claim overlap (C97-C111) on sequence conservation patterns and structural analysis of β-layer-containing proteins. Both evaluations agree these claims are SUPPORTED. Reviewers accept the detailed structural observations and conservation patterns as supporting mechanistic understanding.

Perfect claim overlap (C115) on functional advantages of β-layers for resilience. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct functional studies. Peer reviewers rate as UNSUPPORTED, directly challenging the claim and stating biochemical data on stability is needed to support resilience claims.

High overlap (C50-C71, 21/22 shared claims) on systematic structural characterization of multiple constructs. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on high-resolution structures and biophysical data. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning minimal length requirements and noting GCN4 stabilization may affect generalizability.

High overlap (C31-C32, C76-C83) on the novel alternating α/β architecture. Both evaluations agree these claims are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes novelty and structural characterization; peer reviewers acknowledge the finding and request additional prevalence information but do not challenge the novelty.

High overlap (C72-C75) on alternative conformations and glutamate effects. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on crystal structure data showing two conformations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, specifically citing this finding to question which residues can form β-layers and requesting biochemical validation.

Moderate overlap (C13-C29) on established coiled coil periodicity principles and discontinuities. Both evaluations agree these background claims are SUPPORTED. These represent foundational knowledge from prior work that provides context for novel findings.

Moderate overlap (C2-C3, C30, C39-C42, C44) on primary experimental finding of β-layer formation. Both evaluations agree these claims are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes high-resolution structural data and internal consistency; peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as the core finding showing a new coiled-coil assembly mode.

Moderate overlap (C1, C5-C12) on established coiled coil structure background. Both evaluations agree these claims are SUPPORTED as foundational knowledge from prior work (Crick, Lupas) that provides context for interpreting novel findings.

Partial overlap (C34-C38) on OMP100 structural characterization including CD spectroscopy and thermal stability. Both evaluations agree these claims are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers accept this as part of systematic structural characterization building on previous SadA work.

Minimal overlap (C114) on synthesis of findings within coiled coil structural principles. OpenEval includes this in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of C112-C114. Peer reviewers include C114 in their affirmation of the core finding as SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap (C54, C88) addressing oligomeric state specificity. OpenEval R4 rates structural characterization as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly questioning whether β-layer formation is limited to trimeric parallel coiled coils and noting prediction difficulties.

Minimal overlap (C25) on speculative upper periodicity limit. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of experimental validation and notes most structures have lower periodicities. Peer reviewers include C25 in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of background claims without specific comment.

OpenEval R7 addresses C84-C85 on hexad-spaced β-layers, rating as SUPPORTED based on structural analysis of PDB 2C3F. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims about hexad spacing.

OpenEval R12 addresses C116 on β-layers as substantially novel backbone architecture, rating as SUPPORTED based on Ramachandran analysis and minimal sequence changes required. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific claim.
